progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C1 to C10, G01 and Year 11: ionic compounds are lattices of positive and negative ions; water is polar; endothermic and exothermic; ions and state symbols (Year 11). Dynamic equilibrium with equal rates (C1); a slower rate rising to meet a falling one (C2); Q against K (C8); the K expression with pure solids left out (C5); K changes only with temperature and heating raises K for a heat-absorbing reaction (C9); Ksp named as K for a solid dissolving (C10); spreading out (entropy) as a second factor favouring a change (G01). Not assumed: lattice energy values, Hess cycles, solubility rules.
progression.startsWith: A blue copper sulfate crystal dissolving in water, with the question of what pulls the ions out of the crystal and why some salts make water hot while others make it cold.
progression.stopsAfter: Describing hydration with ion-dipole attractions; writing a dissociation equation with state symbols; explaining a temperature change on dissolving with both energy steps; saying why an endothermic salt can still dissolve (spreading out); explaining saturation as equal dissolving and crystallising rates, with tracer evidence; predicting the effect of adding solid and adding water on a saturated mixture, and saying why heating dissolves more of a salt that dissolves endothermically. No Ksp calculations, no solubility rules, no lattice energy arithmetic, no Gibbs free energy, no cycad case, no supersaturation.
progression.nextLesson: C12: how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have used solubility to remove toxins from food; then C13: solubility rules and precipitation.

teaching.task: Say what pulls the ions out when an ionic solid dissolves, explain why the water warms or cools, and explain why dissolving in a saturated solution is an equilibrium.
teaching.causalExplanation: The oppositely charged ends of polar water molecules attract the ions, and an exposed corner ion is held by the fewest neighbours, so water pulls ions off the lattice and surrounds them. The ions were already in the crystal, so dissolving only separates and hydrates them. Separating the ions costs energy and hydrating them releases energy, so the sum, the enthalpy of solution, is negative when hydration pays back more and the water warms, and positive when separation costs more and the water cools. A salt that takes in energy can still dissolve because spreading out also favours dissolving. In a saturated solution the dissolving rate is steady while the crystallising rate rises with the number of dissolved ions until the two are equal, so the amounts stay fixed, which is a dynamic equilibrium with its K the Ksp. The solid is left out of K, so adding more changes nothing, while heating changes K itself.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on a dissolving copper sulfate crystal and the hot and cold puzzle, builds the lattice and polar water, shows hydration and the equation, counts energy in two steps with real hot pack and cold pack values, resolves the endothermic puzzle with spreading out, builds saturation as two rates meeting with tracer evidence, adds the added-solid trap, gives two memory aids, then asks two unseen items with a short pause and brief feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: Ions are held tightly in a crystal. What pulls them out into the water, and why do some salts make the water hot while others make it cold?
teaching.understandingCheck: Ammonium chloride dissolves and the water falls from 22 degrees to 17 degrees: explain with the two energy steps. Then water is added to a saturated sodium chloride solution that still has solid at the end, at the same temperature: say what happens to the mass of solid and to the final concentration.
teaching.curriculumScope: Describe and analyse the processes involved in the dissolution of ionic compounds in water (Module 5, C5-IQ4-01). Ksp calculations, solubility rules, lattice energy arithmetic, Gibbs free energy, the cycad case and supersaturation are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the painted copper sulfate beaker pair, the painted unsaturated and saturated beakers, the painted thermometer cues, a coded NaCl lattice with polar water, the coded two-step energy ledger and dH bar chart, the C2 two-rate meter, the C5 left-out tray and the C8 Q against K gauge. Colour key: positive ions amber, negative ions violet, water pale blue with delta marks, energy in warm red, energy out teal, radioactive ions green glow.
design.transitionPlan: The beaker anchors the hook and shrinks to the left column while the lattice close-up opens; the equation strip sits above the close-up; the ledger replaces the close-up and returns small for the bar chart and the aids; the saturated beaker and the rate lens carry the equilibrium scenes; the tray and gauge return for the added-solid trap; each attempt clears the board and its feedback rebuilds the ledger or the gauge; the next chip slides in; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.visualReference: Painted copper sulfate beaker pair (crystal then dissolved, aligned) with the process clip or an interim crossfade, the painted hot thermometer and a cold cue
scenes.teachingReason: Poses the puzzle: a crystal vanishes into even colour, so what pulls ions out of a lattice, and why do some salts warm the water while others cool it
scenes.narrationCue: watch / shrinks / pale blue / hot / cold
scenes.motionPurpose: The crystal beaker plays into the dissolved beaker, a ring marks the shrinking crystal, a tag names the spreading copper ions and two thermometers ask hot or cold
scenes.onScreenChange: Heading "Where does a dissolving crystal go?" writes on; on "watch" the crystal plate plays to the dissolved plate with blue streaks rising; on "shrinks" a pen ring circles the crystal; on "pale blue" the tag "copper ions spread out" writes; on "hot" the hot thermometer stands at the right with a pen "?"; on "cold" the cold cue stands beside it
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second on the two questions

scenes.visualReference: Coded NaCl lattice block with amber sodium and larger violet chloride ions, and one enlarged polar water molecule with delta marks
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the two players before the action: a lattice held by opposite charges and a polar water molecule, each with a plain meaning
scenes.motionPurpose: The beaker shrinks to the left column, the lattice builds ion by ion, one ion links to its neighbours and the water molecule enlarges with its charge marks
scenes.onScreenChange: The beaker shrinks to the left column; on "lattice" the NaCl block builds, one inner Na+ pulses and six pen lines run to its neighbours with the tag "held by every neighbour" and the plain meaning "a regular stack of ions"; on "polar" one water molecule enlarges with delta-minus on the oxygen and delta-plus on each hydrogen and the tag "one end slightly negative, the other slightly positive"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second so both definitions can be read

scenes.visualReference: Lattice close-up filling with pale blue water molecules, with oxygen ends toward sodium and hydrogen ends toward chloride, a corner ion lifting off and a full water shell
scenes.teachingReason: Explains the cause of dissolving: oppositely charged ends pull on the ions, a corner ion is held by the fewest neighbours, and a water shell makes the ion aqueous
scenes.narrationCue: turn to face the ions / ion-dipole attraction / corner / surround it completely / hydrated
scenes.motionPurpose: Water molecules rotate to face the ions, a dashed attraction line pulses, a corner chloride with three neighbour lines lifts off, a shell of six waters closes round it and the aqueous labels land
scenes.onScreenChange: On "turn to face the ions" surface water molecules rotate, oxygen toward Na+ and hydrogen toward Cl-, with a pen arrow on one; on "ion-dipole attraction" a dashed line pulses between a Na+ and a water oxygen and the term and its plain meaning write below; on "corner" a corner Cl- is ringed with three neighbour lines against six inside and lifts off; on "surround it completely" a six-molecule shell closes round it and a Na+ follows; on "hydrated" the labels "Na+(aq)", "Cl-(aq)" and "(aq) = surrounded by water" land
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds on the hydrated ions

scenes.visualReference: Equation strip NaCl(s) to Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq) with the lattice and the drifting hydrated ions side by side and the dissolved copper sulfate beaker in the left column
scenes.teachingReason: Shows that the ions were already in the crystal, so dissolving separates and hydrates them and no salt molecules exist in the water
scenes.narrationCue: sodium ions and chloride ions / separates / no salt molecules
scenes.motionPurpose: The equation writes on with the aqueous labels flying in from the close-up, the lattice and the free ions sit side by side, and a wrong chip about salt molecules is crossed
scenes.onScreenChange: On "sodium ions and chloride ions" the strip writes "NaCl(s) -> Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq)" with the (aq) labels flying in; on "separates" the lattice and the drifting hydrated ions sit side by side with the tag "same ions, now apart"; on "no salt molecules" the chip "NaCl molecules in water" fades in and is crossed with the caption "only separate hydrated ions"; the beaker tag becomes "hydrated Cu2+ = the blue"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second after the crossed chip

scenes.visualReference: Coded two-step energy ledger: a warm red bar rising for separating the ions, a teal bar falling for hydrating them, a net bar and a thermometer column
scenes.teachingReason: Counts the energy in two steps so the sign of their sum explains warming or cooling
scenes.narrationCue: away from each other / goes in / cling to / comes out / both happen together / enthalpy of solution / heats the water / from the water
scenes.motionPurpose: A red bar rises, a teal bar falls from its top, a bracket joins them, a net bar appears, and the thermometer column rises or falls as the longer bar swaps
scenes.onScreenChange: The ledger replaces the close-up; on "away from each other" and "goes in" the red bar rises with the tag "separate the ions: energy in, +"; on "cling to" and "comes out" the teal bar falls with "hydrate the ions: energy out, -"; on "both happen together" a pen bracket joins them with "counted separately, happen together"; on "enthalpy of solution" the net bar shows "dH(solution) = step 1 + step 2"; on "heats the water" the teal bar outgrows the red, the net points down and the column rises; on "from the water" the lengths swap, the net points up and the column falls
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds on the finished ledger

scenes.visualReference: Coded dH bar chart with CaCl2 below zero and NH4NO3 above, mini ledgers, hot pack and cold pack cues and a crossed always-endothermic chip
scenes.teachingReason: Gives real values for both signs and corrects the idea that dissolving always takes in energy
scenes.narrationCue: minus 81 kilojoules per mole / instant hot packs / plus 25.7 / instant cold packs
scenes.motionPurpose: A teal bar drops for calcium chloride, a hot pack cue appears, a red bar rises for ammonium nitrate, a cold pack cue appears and a wrong chip is crossed
scenes.onScreenChange: The chart draws with a zero line and "kJ/mol, 25 C"; on "minus 81 kilojoules per mole" a teal bar drops labelled "calcium chloride, CaCl2: -81" with a mini ledger showing the longer teal bar; on "instant hot packs" the hot pack cue stands under it; on "plus 25.7" a red bar rises labelled "ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3: +25.7" with a mini ledger; on "instant cold packs" the cold pack cue stands under it; the chip "Dissolving always takes in energy" fades in and is crossed with "it can go either way"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds on the two bars

scenes.visualReference: The bar chart kept faint with a tall compressed NaCl ledger, a magnifier ring on the tiny gap and a bracket
scenes.teachingReason: Shows that the difference of two large steps, not either step alone, sets the temperature change
scenes.narrationCue: close to 800 kilojoules per mole / plus 3.9 / difference
scenes.motionPurpose: Two tall bars draw, a magnifier ring zooms the tiny gap between their ends and a bracket marks the difference
scenes.onScreenChange: The earlier bars fade back; on "close to 800 kilojoules per mole" a tall NaCl ledger draws with a red bar up "about +800" and a teal bar down "about -800"; on "plus 3.9" a magnifier ring zooms the gap labelled "NaCl: +3.9 (measured)" with the screen tag "1 mol in 1 L: under 1 C cooler"; on "difference" a pen bracket spans the gap with "difference decides"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds on the magnified gap

scenes.visualReference: Two-pan balance sketch with an energy cost pan and a spreading out pan, an ordered-to-scattered ion inset and a crossed big-cost chip
scenes.teachingReason: Resolves the puzzle of an endothermic salt that still dissolves by recalling spreading out from the earlier video
scenes.narrationCue: releasing heat / spreading out / increase in entropy / wins
scenes.motionPurpose: The balance sketch writes, the ordered lattice scatters into a wide field of water, the balance tips toward spreading out and a wrong chip is crossed
scenes.onScreenChange: The cold pack cue and its red bar return small; on "releasing heat" and "spreading out" the balance writes with left pan "energy: +25.7 (against)" and right pan "spreading out (entropy): for"; on "increase in entropy" an inset shows ordered amber and violet ions scattering through water; on "wins" the balance tips with "NH4NO3 dissolves anyway"; on the closing sentence the chip "big dH cost = won't dissolve" fades in and is crossed

scenes.visualReference: Painted unsaturated and saturated beaker pair (aligned) with coded crystals falling in and a stopped question tag
scenes.teachingReason: Defines unsaturated and saturated by what is seen, then asks whether dissolving has really stopped
scenes.motionPurpose: Crystals fall in and vanish, the beaker crossfades to the saturated plate with solid on the bottom, and a pen tag asks whether dissolving stopped
scenes.onScreenChange: The unsaturated plate shows with the label "unsaturated: all the solid dissolves" and coded crystals falling in and vanishing; on "saturated" it crossfades to the saturated plate with the label "saturated: the most it can hold at this temperature"; on "stopped" the pen tag "stopped?" hangs on the crystals
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second on the question

scenes.visualReference: Lens on the crystal surface with leaving and joining ions, a two-rate meter, the equation strip morphing to a two-way arrow and the left-out tray
scenes.teachingReason: Explains why dissolving seems to stop: a steady dissolving rate is met by a rising crystallising rate until they are equal
scenes.narrationCue: leaving / bump into / speeds up / equal / two-way arrow / Ksp
scenes.motionPurpose: Ions leave at a steady count and dissolved ions join the surface, the crystallising bar climbs to meet the flat dissolving bar, the arrow becomes two-way and the solid drops into the left-out tray
scenes.onScreenChange: A lens opens on the saturated crystal; on "leaving" hydrated ions leave steadily; on "bump into" a dissolved ion hits and joins with the tag "crystallising"; the meter shows a flat "dissolving rate" and a low "crystallising rate"; on "speeds up" the dissolved count rises and the crystallising bar climbs; on "equal" the bars meet with a teal "=" and "equal rates, not stopped"; on "two-way arrow" the strip becomes "NaCl(s) <=> Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq)"; on "Ksp" the NaCl(s) tile drops into the tray and "Ksp = [Na+][Cl-]" writes small with "calculations: later video"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds on the equal bars

scenes.visualReference: Saturated beaker plate with a small crystal of green-glowing ions, steady mass and concentration readouts and a rising radioactivity meter
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the evidence that ions keep swapping in a saturated solution while the amounts stay fixed
scenes.motionPurpose: A glowing crystal drops on the pile, the readouts stay fixed, glowing ions appear in the liquid and the radioactivity meter rises, then plain ions dock where glowing ones left
scenes.onScreenChange: The beaker shows "saturated potassium bromide, KBr"; on "radioactive" a small crystal with green-glowing ions drops onto the pile with the tag "radioactive ions: a detector can track them" and the readouts "mass of solid: same", "concentration: same" hold; on "in the solution" glowing hydrated ions appear one by one in a lens and the "radioactivity in solution" meter rises from zero; on "rejoining" plain ions dock where glowing ones left and the two-way arrows light
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second on the steady readouts

scenes.visualReference: Saturated beaker with a growing pile, the left-out tray with a second solid tile, a small Q against K gauge unmoved and a KNO3 warming panel
scenes.teachingReason: Blocks the trap that adding solid shifts the equilibrium, and contrasts it with temperature, which changes K itself
scenes.narrationCue: more salt / left out / equals K / warming
scenes.motionPurpose: Crystals tumble onto the pile while the concentration readout stays fixed, a second solid tile drops into the tray, the gauge pointer stays on the K notch and the KNO3 pile shrinks as it warms
scenes.onScreenChange: On "more salt" coded crystals tumble onto the pile with "concentration: same"; on "left out" the tray returns with NaCl(s) in it and a second solid tile drops beside it; on "equals K" the gauge shows Q on the K notch with the tag "added solid: no shift"; on "warming" a second panel relabels the beaker "KNO3, dissolving endothermic", shows "heat-absorbing: heat it, K rises", shrinks the pile and tags "about 32 g per 100 g water at 20 C; about 64 g at 40 C"
